dedupe_keys.name: iowa agent based model of regional food hub disintermediation with reinforcement learning

description: This case study models a risk to regional food systems in Iowa, United States: food hubs, which provide logistics for small and mid-sized farms, being cut out once farmers sell directly to the customers the hub found for them. Teri J. Craven and Caroline C. Krejci of Iowa State University presented it at the 2017 Spring Simulation Multi-Conference in the Agent-Directed Simulation Symposium. Their agent-based model uses reinforcement learning to represent producer decisions on selling through the hub or directly, in a regional food supply network in Iowa, and is meant as a decision support tool for hub managers to test supply chain management strategies and their effect on producers and long-term system success. The conference paper is available online from the Society for Modeling and Simulation International by purchase; its abstract is free in OpenAlex. Coverage is one regional network. Caveats: the model code and calibration data are not published, and the abstract gives no quantitative results. The authors warn that widespread disintermediation can lead to hub failure, which can disrupt the whole regional food system. Simulation uses: producer behaviour rules and a hub failure mechanism for agent-based models of local food supply resilience. Related records: the USDA local food directories (data-usda-local-food-directories) list food hubs across the United States.
